title: Cascading swallowing of outer paragraphs into quotation sidecars due to strict 'number != expected' clause

corpus_scope.description: At least 1,632 out of 7,708 cases exhibit outer sequence cascading swallowing caused by non-consecutive numbering.

primary_example.text_evidence:
...interpret the scope of section 97 of the Act, and this interpretation involves a question of law, which is subject to the correctness standard.
[37]
Accordingly, I will apply the correctness standard to the section 97 interpretation and the reasonableness standard to the panel's findings of fact.
Summary
[38]
The Court is of the view that consideration of an application for protected person status...

current_behavior: In pipeline_v2/source/core.py lines 123-127, 'nested' is assigned True if '(number != expected and not reset)'. When a judge or court reporter skips a single paragraph number (e.g. [35] jumps to [37] in 000758.txt), expected is 36, number is 37 != 36. [37] is classified as nested quotation sidecar. quote_active is set to True, and last_outer remains stuck at 35. For every subsequent paragraph [38], [39]... [75], number != 36 is continuously True, causing all remaining 37 paragraphs (over 25,000 bytes) and headings to be swallowed into a single outer paragraph unit [35].
expected_behavior: Paragraph numbering gaps (e.g. 35 -> 37, 6 -> 8) must be recognized as outer sequence progression. A marker without a preceding quotation cue (intro) and without indentation should advance outer numbering (with an uncertainty flag like 'numbering_gap_observed'), rather than permanently freezing last_outer and swallowing all subsequent text as quotation sidecars.
m2_impact: BLOCKER for M2. Retrieval core chunking in M2 relies on paragraph boundaries. When 21.17% of the corpus has giant paragraphs of 20,000-50,000 bytes with 30-70 swallowed outer paragraphs, M2 cannot respect legal paragraph units. Core chunks will either be forced into length fallback splits spanning multiple distinct legal analyses, or lose structural unit indexing entirely. In bilingual cases (000432.txt, 014069.txt), whole French versions are swallowed into English paragraphs.
minimal_fix_direction: 1. Remove '(number != expected and not reset)' as an unconditional cause for 'nested = True'. Require evidence of nesting (e.g. intro is True, or indent > root_indent, or quotation block context). 2. If number > last_outer without quotation cues, advance last_outer = number, reset quote_active = False, and record 'numbering_gap_observed' in uncertainties. 3. Allow numbering resets to trigger even if [1] is absent when bilingual separators or French cues appear.

title: False numbering reset triggered by body quotation starting with [1], corrupting language region and swallowing English text

corpus_scope.description: 62 cases in summary.json report 'numbering_reset_language_unknown'. In cases like 050936, this is caused by body quotations.

primary_example.text_evidence:
[30]
The Board is entitled to draw reasonable conclusions with respect to credibility based on implausibility... As noted by Justice Shore in <FRAGMENT_SUPPRESSED> [2007] FCJ No 97:
[1] The Court is of the opinion that the Board may draw reasonable conclusions based on implausibilities, common sense and rationality and may reject testimony if it does not accord with the probabilities affecting the case as a whole: (
 <FRAGMENT_SUPPRESSED>  (QL))
[31]
The jurisprudence has established that internal inconsistencies in an applicant's story...

current_behavior: In pipeline_v2/source/core.py line 117, 'reset = number == 1 and last_outer is not None and last_outer > 1'. When paragraph 30 quotes paragraph [1] of an external decision introduced by 'As noted by Justice Shore in ...:', QUOTE_CUE fails to match ('noted' is not in regex). Because number == 1, 'reset' is True, and 'nested' evaluates to False. The parser resets outer sequence to 1, sets language_region to 'unknown:1'. When real outer paragraph [31] arrives, expected is 2, so [31] through [54] are treated as nested sidecars under the quoted [1] unit. Furthermore, when the actual French translation appears at [2], it is absorbed into this 'unknown:1' sequence.
expected_behavior: A marker [1] occurring inside a paragraph preceded by a citation colon or quote intro must be classified as a quoted marker sidecar, not a document-level translation/numbering reset. Document resets require separation cues (e.g. rule lines, [traduction], or full header blocks), or should at least verify that following paragraphs do not immediately resume the prior outer sequence ([31]).
m2_impact: BLOCKER for M2. Paragraphs 31-54 of English text are hidden as sidecars under an 'unknown:1' unit, and subsequent French text is mislabeled as unknown:1. Chunks in M2 will mix languages and lose outer paragraph boundaries.
minimal_fix_direction: 1. Expand quote intro detection to include common introduction patterns (citations ending in colon, 'noted', 'observed'). 2. In line 117, do not trigger numbering reset if the [1] line is immediately preceded by an active paragraph or citation cue without section break / translation separator. 3. If a subsequent marker matches last_outer + 1 (e.g. [31] following [30]), discard the candidate reset and treat [1] as quoted.

title: False positive headings from header metadata and headnote classification lines

corpus_scope.description: 4,246 units in summary.json have 'heading_candidate'. A significant fraction are court headers and headnote topic lines.

current_behavior: In pipeline_v2/source/core.py lines 152-156, 'title_candidate = previous_blank and len(clean) <= 100 and len(clean.split()) >= 2 and clean.istitle() and not re.search(r'[.;,!?]$', clean)'. Header lines such as 'Federal Court', 'Trial Division' and headnote catalog lines like 'Aliens - Topic 2' satisfy this condition and are created as structural 'heading' units. Consequently, 'section_path_refs' for all body paragraphs in the entire case point to 'Federal Court' or topic lines.
expected_behavior: Lines preceding the first paragraph that match known court names or headnote topic classification patterns should remain part of the unnumbered header block, rather than becoming structural section headings.
m2_impact: MEDIUM to HIGH in M2. In M2 hybrid retrieval and dense prefix generation, section_refs are attached to passages (e.g. prefixing chunk with heading). Attaching 'Federal Court' or 'Aliens - Topic 2' or 'Defences - Consent - [See' as section heading pollutes chunk embedding representations and BM25 field boost.
minimal_fix_direction: Exclude header lines (before first paragraph) matching court names or 'Topic [0-9]' from title_candidate headings.

title: False negative headings: ALL CAPS legal headings (ORDER, INTRODUCTION, ARGUMENTS) excluded by case-sensitive heuristic

corpus_scope.sample_statistic: In a 500-case sample, ORDER was missed in 78 cases (15.6%), INTRODUCTION in 23 cases, ARGUMENTS in 12 cases.
corpus_scope.description: Standard Canadian judgment ALL CAPS section headings not in KNOWN_HEADING fail clean.istitle() and split() >= 2.

primary_example.text_evidence:
Summary
[38]
The Court is of the view...
primary_example.additional_evidence: Standalone 'ORDER', 'INTRODUCTION', 'DECISION', 'STATUTORY PROVISIONS' lines across the corpus.

current_behavior: KNOWN_HEADING regex contains only 18 specific keywords. All other candidate headings must pass 'clean.istitle()' and 'len(clean.split()) >= 2'. Single-word uppercase headings like 'ORDER', 'INTRODUCTION', 'ARGUMENTS', 'LEGISLATION' fail both conditions and are omitted from heading events.
expected_behavior: Prominent standalone section headers in uppercase or title case should be recognized as headings or heading candidates.
m2_impact: MODERATE in M2. M2 section boundary splitting and reading context references will miss genuine section breaks such as 'ORDER' or 'INTRODUCTION', causing chunks to merge introductory remarks or orders into body paragraphs.
minimal_fix_direction: Expand KNOWN_HEADING to include 'order', 'ordonnance', 'introduction', 'arguments', 'legislation', 'motifs', and allow single-word uppercase lines if isolated by blank lines.

title: Tautological bundle validation: validator re-runs identical builder heuristic without independent structural assertions

corpus_scope.description: The validation harness tests algorithm reproducibility rather than structural correctness.

primary_example.code_lines: Line 229: if record != parse_source(ident, raw, self.manifest['profile']): raise M1Error(...)

current_behavior: validate_bundle() iterates over all sources and calls parse_source(ident, raw, profile), checking record == fresh. If parse_source has an algorithmic defect (e.g. swallowing 37 paragraphs in 000758.txt), fresh produces the identical defect, and the equality check evaluates to True. The test suite thus certified 100% PASS (21/21 tests, 7,708/7,708 sources) despite widespread cascading defects.
expected_behavior: Bundle validation should assert independent invariant properties: e.g., that sidecars do not form long ascending outer sequences, that paragraphs do not exceed abnormal length thresholds without flags, and that headings inside swallowed regions are detected.
m2_impact: METHODOLOGY / GOVERNANCE IMPACT. Masked the 1,632 corrupted cases from detection prior to M1 sign-off.
minimal_fix_direction: Incorporate structural sanity checks into validate_bundle (e.g. max sidecars per parent with ascending markers, presence of unparented sidecars in unnumbered regions).

title: Header literal metadata regex collects all neutral citations in header, including cited authorities in headnotes

corpus_scope.description: Cases where headnotes or summaries precede paragraph [1] and cite prior decisions.

current_behavior: re.finditer on neutral citation pattern extracts all citations in header. In 042691.txt, both the case's citation and citations of cases in headnote are collected as candidates with 'observed_not_identity_verified'.
expected_behavior: Acceptable per M1 contract: M1 explicitly specifies that metadata consists of literal observations, not verified case identity, and leaves resolution to downstream stages.
m2_impact: LOW for M2. M2 does not rely on metadata citation for chunking; case identity is maintained via M0 inventory case_id.
minimal_fix_direction: Retain as documented limitation. Document in M2 ingestion profile.

title: Legitimate unnumbered blocks (headers, titles, counsel tables) correctly labeled as structure_unknown

corpus_scope.description: Normal court cases where 0-2% of bytes are header metadata and unnumbered preliminary notes.

current_behavior: Text preceding paragraph [1] that is not a heading (e.g. style of cause, counsel, judges) is kept in an unnumbered unit with uncertainty ['structure_unknown'].
expected_behavior: Acceptable per M1 contract: 5.70% unnumbered bytes across corpus is not 5.70% error. Valid court headers are legitimately unnumbered.
reproduction_command: None needed; verified across random sample cases.
m2_impact: NONE. M2 can safely exclude or treat header unnumbered units as non-core context according to policy.
